item.title: Lumbar Central / Unilateral PA Mobilization
clinicalUse: Selected non-specific low-back pain with a positive comparable sign
patientPosition: Prone with pillow under abdomen if needed for comfort.
therapistPosition: Stand beside the patient at the target level.
Keep wrists neutral and use controlled body weight.
stabilization: Pelvis remains supported by the table.
Avoid creating excessive global lumbar extension.
contact: Central PA over spinous process using hypothenar/thumb contact.
Unilateral PA over the relevant posterior element with a broad contact.
forceDirection: Grade and amplitude are selected from irritability and stiffness.
steps: 2. Screen serious pathology and neurological red flags.
6. Follow with active movement or loading.
mistakes: Using PA mobilization despite progressive neurological signs.
Treating imaging findings rather than the patient's comparable sign.
safety: Do not use routine manual treatment when cauda equina, fracture, infection or malignancy is suspected.
item.visualCue: Lumbar spinous contact → PA force → Re-test lumbar movement/function.

subTechniques.name: Lumbar Central PA Mobilization
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Pain modulation or extension tolerance in selected mechanical low-back presentations.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Prone with a pillow under the abdomen if it improves comfort.
subTechniques.contact: Broad hypothenar/supported-thumb contact over the selected spinous process with wrists neutral.
subTechniques.direction: Apply a controlled posterior-to-anterior oscillation through the selected level.
subTechniques.dosage: 30–60 seconds × 2–4 bouts with re-test after each bout.
subTechniques.reassess: Lumbar extension/flexion, sit-to-stand and symptom distribution.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Treat the comparable sign, not the imaging level. A stiff-feeling segment is not automatically the pain source.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Do not use routine manual therapy when cauda equina, fracture, infection or malignancy is suspected.

subTechniques.name: Lumbar Unilateral PA Mobilization
subTechniques.target: Lumbar posterior element on the selected side
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve selected rotation/side-bending restriction or local pain when unilateral loading is helpful.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Prone with pelvis level and trunk relaxed.
subTechniques.contact: Broad contact over the posterior element while the opposite hand supports the mobilizing hand.
subTechniques.direction: Apply a unilateral posterior-to-anterior oscillation, avoiding global lumbar extension.
subTechniques.reassess: Rotation/side-bending and the functional movement that reproduced pain.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: If leg symptoms spread farther distally, stop and reassess rather than progressing the grade.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid progressive neurological loss or red-flag spinal presentations.
